I'm surprised nobody hit on what I see as the most obvious reason for this by far: the NSA.

After Snowden any country that values their privacy would basically be insane to work with US companies, hardware, or software. China, now the largest economy in the world, has openly banned Windows 8 on government computers. Other countries are certainly following in their lead, if keeping it somewhat more low key.

Going open source is an interesting way for Microsoft to fight the NSA. Any illicit "extraneous code" would be vastly easier to uncover in open source software. More legitimate "extraneous code" could be completely disabled or refactored to ensure security. And it's trivial to check if the executable binaries being run are the same binaries produced by the source code being provided. It's win win for everybody. Open source as an aside doesn't mean "free." Microsoft can still maintain copyright on all assets related to their software. What that means is you may have the code that "is" windows, but it wouldn't actually run windows without access to Microsoft's copyrighted components. This, for instance, is how some video game companies have managed to release their products as open source yet still maintain commercial control of their product.
